div.head: Ps Cn for 1
div.ab: Sint iam deinceps quatuor ex liberalioribus hominibus, qui habent saluas suas debitas consuetudines, quos Angli þegenes appellant, in qualibet regni mei prouincia constituti ad iusticiam distribuendam una cum pena merita pro materiis foreste cuncto populo meo, tam Anglis quam Danis, per totum regnum meum Anglie, quos quatuor primarios foreste appellandos censemus.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 620 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: Let there henceforth be four of the nobler men, who have their due customs secured, whom the English call þegenes (thegns), appointed in each province of my realm to dispense justice, together with deserved punishment, in matters of the forest to all my people, English as well as Danes, throughout my whole realm of England; and we decree that these four are to be called the chief men of the forest.

note.seg: sog. Benedictus Gesta Henr. II (ed. Stubbs I 323) erzählt zu 1184: Rex diuisit forestas .. in plures partes et unicuique parti præfecit IV iusticiarios .. et constituit .. II seruientes custodes uenationis et uiridis. Solch ein Colleg kommt sonst nicht vor, vielmehr unterstand die Forstverwaltung vor- und nachher Einem summus (capitalis, magister, proto-)forestarius (iustitiarius forestæ), seit 1238 je einem nördl. und südl. vom Trentflusse; vgl. Turner Sel. pleas of the forest p. xv

The so-called Benedictus, Gesta Henr. II (ed. Stubbs I 323), relates under 1184: Rex diuisit forestas .. in plures partes et unicuique parti præfecit IV iusticiarios .. et constituit .. II seruientes custodes uenationis et uiridis. Such a board occurs nowhere else; rather, the forest administration before and after was under one summus (capitalis, magister, proto-)forestarius (iustitiarius forestæ), from 1238 one each north and south of the river Trent; cf. Turner, Sel. pleas of the forest p. xv.

im Gegensatz zu mediocres und minuti. Unten 34 identificirt sie Verf. mit den twelfhynde men. Er wünscht die Oberforstmeister dem Adel entnommen, was regelmässig geschah; wenn er je den der Grafschaft, und nur weltlichen, zu Forstrichtern will, so widersprach das der Wirklichkeit; durch Grossgrundbesitz und Wahl hingen je mit der Grafschaft, wo sie amtirten, zusammen die uiridarii; s. u. 2. Die Dreitheilung der Volksstände und die der Forsthierarchie entsprechen nicht der Wirklichkeit. Verf. verräth baroniale Tendenz und tadelt die Härte gegen das untere Volk nicht

As opposed to mediocres and minuti. Below, 34, the author identifies them with the twelfhynde men. He wants the chief foresters taken from the nobility, which regularly happened; when he wants as forest judges in each case men of the shire, and only laymen, that contradicted reality; it was the uiridarii who, through large landholding and election, were connected with the shire in which they served; see below, 2. The threefold division of the ranks of the people and that of the forest hierarchy do not correspond to reality. The author betrays a baronial tendency and does not censure the harshness toward the lower people.

der Verf. — wohl höherer Forstbeamter, vom Adel — stiehlt Cnuts Namen und fälscht dessen Worte, die er nur aus Instituta Cnuti (o. S. 612, und zwar der Classe H) kennt. Er arbeitet 1130—1217, wahrscheinlich um 1185; vgl. Liebermann Über Pseudo-Cnuts Const. de foresta (Halle 1894). Gemäss der Dänischen Maske spricht Verf. zu Danis 1, vergisst sie aber, als Compilator redend: censemus (1 Ende), antiquo (21)

The author (probably a higher forest official, of noble rank) steals Cnut's name and forges his words, which he knows only from the Instituta Cnuti (above, p. 612, and specifically of class H). He works between 1130 and 1217, probably c. 1185; cf. Liebermann, Über Pseudo-Cnuts Const. de foresta (Halle 1894). In keeping with his Danish mask the author says Danis (1), but forgets it when speaking as compiler: censemus (end of 1), antiquo (21).

Verf. meint, laut des Zusatzes, nicht die Reichsmagnaten, sondern vielleicht die Oberförster in 1. Vgl. forestarum per comitatum Berkescire primas unter Heinrich I. (Chron. Abingdon. II 7), was aber kein Amtstitel ist, wie auch primores für die Constituenten des Grafschaftsgerichts (ebd. 120) nicht technisch lautet

To judge by the addition, the author means not the magnates of the realm but perhaps the chief foresters in 1. Cf. forestarum per comitatum Berkescire primas under Henry I (Chron. Abingdon. II 7), which however is not an official title, just as primores for the members of the shire court (ibid. 120) is not a technical term.
